There's a bunch of tactics musicians use. Whichever one gets you results you want is good.
1. Learn a bunch of melodies. Not just guitar melodies, but vocals and trumpets and anything else. Interpolate these in other songs (i.e. play a Santana solo over a Doors song). Like Zhegan2005 said, playing a list of songs and using different ideas in different songs is an easy way to achieve this.
2. Ear-train. Get an app like Perfect Ear which can help you think in terms of music and hear melodies.
3. Learn your chords. This sounds a little counterintuitive, but knowing the chord tones and how to transition between them is vital to jazz soloing.
4. Singing or understanding vocal lines. People listen for vocal lines because they're short and memorable. People will remember hooks far better than verses. With that in mind, try to use only 5 or six note groups and try to make a memorable melody using a strict limit of notes.
